correctness.rationale: For every N>=2,m>=1, the binomial second moment yields exact positive interior p_i,q_i. The harmonic equation gives q_i/p_i=[m(N-i)+i]/[mi+N-i] and the unique absorption probability with symmetric Gamma weights. Differentiating each finite product proves strict one-mutant monotonicity for N>=3 and the endpoint bounds; m=1,N=2 are checked separately. With a=N/(m-1)/N>0 fixed, Stirling and the unique strictly concave maximum phi(1/2)=I_m give both the positive exponential rate and the correct square-root prefactor. Standalone verify.py evaluated 2863 exact or independently computed cases, including matrix solutions; finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The finite encounter group size is a motivated primitive of the primary stochastic social-learning model. This theorem sharply separates one-contact neutral survival 1/N from exponentially rare one-mutant fixation for any fixed m>=2, and gives the exact exposure-size-dependent exponent and pre-exponential constant. This establishes a meaningful finite-population invasion benchmark, not just a toy enumeration or renaming of a known phase.
